snippet.title: The Cactus Magazine - Chrome Dino IRL part 3
snippet.description:
The Cactus Magazine - Chrome Dino IRL Part 3
•••
The obstacles magnet onto the 3D printed conveyor belt, and if they just rode around in a loop the game would be the same sequence forever. So at the end of the belt, these ramps passively pull each obstacle off and drop it into a ten-sided indexing wheel. Every drop ratchets the wheel forward one slot, which pushes the next obstacle up to the top of the queue, ready to go back into the game.
•••
The original plan was a gantry-style pick-and-place that would grab obstacles and set them on the moving belt, but the obstacles are all different sizes, so it would've needed a vision system just to find them, plus a gripper synced to a moving conveyor. The indexing wheel does the same job with fewer moving parts.
•••
The end goal is three of these magazines side by side with a randomizer picking which one serves up the next obstacle, so the sequence never repeats. Stay tuned for that!
•••

snippet.title: Man Turns WWII-Era Stone Ruin Into Dream Home In Just One Year | Start To Finish @luxonbushcraft
snippet.description:
Deep in a wooded mountain landscape stands a house that shouldn't have been ordinary. 

And wasn't. 

Built in 1957, more than a decade after World War II officially ended, it is, in every practical sense, still a product of that war. Because a conflict of that scale doesn't end with a signed treaty. It ends slowly, in shortages, in scars, in the quiet resourcefulness of a generation rebuilding its world one salvaged stone at a time.

By the time this house rose from the ground, Europe was still finding its feet. Materials were scarce and often recycled and skilled hands were rarer still, as an entire generation of tradesmen had vanished into the war, leaving construction to determined amateurs who built on instinct rather than training. 

As you see, the result was a house without pretense: practical, honest, built to survive rather than impress.

Indeed, that history is written into every wall. 

Now, working completely alone and off-grid, Luxon takes it on, battling failing roofs, crumbling masonry and a punishing mountain terrain to bring the house (and its history) back to life. 

Luxon Bushcraft

snippet.title: Smooth Conveyor Belt Build - Chrome Dino Game IRL
snippet.description:
Building an Infinite Floor for a Real-Life Chrome Dino Game
•••
Before the dino can jump over anything, I needed the ground to scroll forever. So I built a 56-segment 3D printed conveyor belt with embedded magnets for the obstacles. The belt runs on an aluminum extrusion spine, but the panels were drooping between the drive wheels, so I added V-wheels to each segment that ride along guide rails and turn it into a smooth, solid playing surface. A NEMA 23 motor drives the belt, and a sliding tensioner keeps everything tight so the panels don’t skip. Now the floor scrolls by satisfyingly smooth. Next step: make the dino jump.
•••

snippet.title: Why You Can’t Pee On Antarctica
snippet.description:
In Antarctica, you’re NOT ALLOWED to pee on the ice. Not even when you’re hiking for hours!

It’s so cold and dry that when it snows, it basically never melts, so it stacks up into layers of ice trapping air inside…and scientists drill ice cores to study that air and learn what the environment was like thousands of years ago 

So if you pee…it will get trapped in the ice too.

To see what’s under the ice, subscribe!

snippet.title: University of Waterloo Students Just Broke a Rocket World Record 🚀
snippet.description:
Canadian university students just made rocket history! 🚀🇨🇦

The University of Waterloo Rocketry Team launched Polaris, a student-built liquid bi-propellant rocket, to an incredible altitude of 63,497 feet — about 19.35 km above Earth.

The flight broke the previous world record of 56,590 feet, making Polaris the highest-flying amateur liquid rocket ever launched.

The 17-foot rocket was designed and built by students and successfully recovered after its record-breaking flight.

snippet.title: Añadió Sal al Agua… y el Sonido Cambió por Completo 😳🌊 #shorts
snippet.description:
Este hombre muestra por qué el océano puede sonar tan inquietante. Cuando golpea un gong y lo sumerge en agua dulce, el sonido casi desaparece al instante. Pero luego añade sal al agua… y todo cambia.
Esto ocurre porque en el agua salada, las ondas sonoras de baja frecuencia se comportan de manera diferente, permitiendo que el sonido viaje mucho más lejos y creando un efecto completamente distinto.

snippet.title: Man Builds Stunning SWIMMING POOL In His Backyard | Start To Finish By @EricLeCarreleur
snippet.description:
Are you ready to witness the construction of an in-ground swimming pool from scratch, carried out step by step with professional-level precision? 

What appears, at first glance, to be a simple backyard addition quickly reveals itself as a highly technical build; because a pool is not just an excavation filled with water, but a sealed concrete structure, a hydraulic network, a filtration system, and a finished surface that must withstand constant pressure and permanent immersion.

This build is led by Eric Le Carreleur, whose expertise in tiling defines the approach taken throughout the project. While his trade usually focuses on the final layer, here the logic is reversed: the entire structure is designed and constructed to meet the demands of the finish. This means controlling everything, from ground preparation, drainage, and structural stability to waterproofing and circulation, so that the final surface is not just visually precise, but technically reliable over time.

As the project unfolds, the pool takes shape not as a single structure, but as a sequence of interdependent systems. The excavation defines the geometry, the concrete base provides stability, the walls contain pressure, the waterproofing ensures durability, and the hydraulic network brings the pool to life. 

Each phase builds on the previous one, leaving no room for approximation. What emerges is a fully engineered installation that will make every summer less hot.

Eric Le Carreleur

snippet.title: What's Hidden Under Antarctica?
snippet.description:
Something's hiding below the ice in Antarctica…. 
For optimistic science and tech stories, subscribe!

In 1970, a team of Soviet scientists started drilling. For 28 years, they kept going… until after nearly 4,000 meters… they suddenly stopped. Because they’d found something unimaginable: Liquid water. A secret lake, down below all this ice, that had been completely sealed off from the rest of the world for 15 million years. 

How? And… is there something alive in there? Creatures that have been evolving separately from the rest of the planet for 15 million years?

Scientists started searching for more of these secret lakes, and as they did, they realized there is way more going on under Antarctica than we ever thought.

I needed to know the truth about Earth’s most remote continent. So I've come all the way to Antarctica to show you what's really happening down below this ice. And exactly what they discovered when they finally broke inside…

Something's hiding below the ice in Antarctica…. 
For optimistic science and tech stories, subscribe!

Scientists started searching for more of these secret lakes, and as they did, they realized there is way more going on under Antarctica than we ever thought.

snippet.title: The First Ever Footage of a Giant Squid
snippet.description:
This is the first ever footage of a giant squid in its natural habitat. It took decades to get this footage. And some creative engineering.

The further down into the ocean you go the darker it gets, so when scientists make their way down there with ROV’s or subs the lights and motors typically cause animals adapted for cold, dark isolation to flee. 

In 2012, one scientist got creative and finally caught some incredible footage of a deep sea creature we’d never seen before in its natural habitat. For more, subscribe!

snippet.title: The Most Well Preserved Mummy Ever Found
snippet.description:
This is the most well preserved human ever found. 3… 2… 1… 

In 1972, archaeologists uncovered a meticulously designed tomb. Inside was a woman from around 168 BC that was remarkably well preserved, with traces of blood still in her veins.

We still don’t know exactly how it was done, but it’s a surprising contrast to one of the most well-known methods of mummification. By comparison, Egyptian mummification is a very specific process of embalming. 

Both methods have taught us so much about a world long past, from the diets to the diseases that plagued ancient cultures. The difference? This one left a body so fresh that researchers could perform an autopsy!

For more, subscribe!

snippet.title: Solución de hielo LG: Encantado de conocerte, hielo. | El hielo adecuado para cada momento

✓La solución de hielo LG para el hogar brinda varios tipo de hielo- Esférico, Cubos y triturado- en un mismo refrigerador.
✓ SlimSpacePlus™ libera espacio en el etrepaño manteniendo el hielo rápido y fácil de acceder.
✓ UVnano™ y un filtro de agua certificado por NSF mantiene cada vertido limpio y fresco.

Alto. Olvídate del hielo que conoces. 🧊

Porque quieres hielo que se adapte a tu estilo, no al revés. La solución de hielo LG se construyó sobre esa única idea: ofrecer la experiencia de hielo adecuada mientras se crea más espacio para las cosas que amas, todo comenzando con agua pura y fresca.

Ya sea que estés relajándote después de un largo día, recibiendo a familiares y amigos, o simplemente manteniéndote fresco durante todo el día, la solución de hielo LG proporciona el hielo adecuado para el momento adecuado. 

Hielo esférico Craft Ice, hielo triturado, Mini Craft Ice y hielo en cubos cada día están cuidadosamente diseñados para adaptarse a diferentes estilos de vida y ocasiones. 

Y como la propia máquina de hielo está diseñada de manera delgada (esa es la diferencia SlimSpacePlus™), tu refrigerador mantiene su espacio. 

Sin compromisos, sin desorden. Solo acceso rápido y fácil al hielo siempre que lo necesites. Cada pieza comienza de la misma manera: filtrada a través de un filtro de agua certificado por NSF, con la boquilla del dispensador mantenida fresca gracias a la tecnología de autocuidado UVnano™.

Porque el hielo no es solo hielo. Es parte de los momentos que hacen la vida cotidiana más agradable. Ice to meet you

snippet.title: How a 5-Ton Temple Bell Is Forged to Ring for 1,000 Years | by @kingprocess
snippet.description:
Only six workshops in the world are capable of forging a 5-ton Buddhist temple bell designed to resonate for a millennium. This video documents the high-stakes, 90-day journey of turning raw bronze and sand into a sacred masterpiece. You’ll witness the painstaking work of hand-carving thousands of characters into wax, the massive engineering of the resin-sand molds, and the high-pressure moment of the 2,100°F pour. From the intricate lost-wax casting of the dragon crown to the final strike that determines if the bell is a success or scrap metal, every second demands absolute precision.

This is for anyone who loves heavy engineering, ancient craftsmanship, or seeing how the world's most massive and rare objects are built.

His work reveals an intuitive understanding of structure, load distribution, and environmental conditions, allowing him to transform irregular, natural materials into a coherent and highly efficient system.

As the project evolves, the cabin becomes a reflection of the builder’s philosophy. Nothing is wasted, and nothing is added without purpose. Offcuts are reused, spaces are optimized, and even the smallest details are carefully considered.

snippet.title: Venda sua torre de purga - Como remover a torre de purga na impressão 3D
snippet.description:
Criado por: @3d.humbe
Traduzido por: @hugolopes3d & @stlflix_

🗑️ Todos nós odiamos as torres de purga na impressão 3D multicolorida.
Modelos: @stlflix_br

🖨️ É aquele bloco de plástico que aparece ao lado da peça toda vez que a impressora troca de cor.
E embora pareçam um desperdício inútil, na verdade cumprem uma função essencial: ajudam a limpar a cor anterior e estabilizar o fluxo do filamento antes de continuar imprimindo.

🌈 Porque numa impressão multicolorida com um único bico, a impressora não troca de cor magicamente.
Dentro do hotend ainda resta material derretido da cor anterior, e se não for purgado corretamente, surgem defeitos, manchas, falhas e problemas de extrusão na peça final.

⚙️ Mas o interessante é que essa purga nem sempre precisa ir para uma torre inútil.
Existe uma função que permite usar um objeto de sacrifício, ou seja, outra peça onde a impressora pode purgar enquanto imprime.

🔥 E se escolhermos bem esse objeto, podemos transformar um desperdício em um subproduto útil, decorativo ou até vendável.
Neste caso, sacrificamos uma ilusão de óptica impressa em 3D.

Então, em vez de terminar com uma torre de plástico sem uso, terminamos com uma peça extra aproveitando o material que normalmente jogaríamos fora.
♻️ Não elimina completamente a purga, mas muda a forma de enxergá-la: de lixo… a oportunidade.

snippet.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: Understanding the human genome
snippet.description:
We’ve used AlphaGenome to predict the molecular impact of every possible single-letter change in the human genome. All nine billion of them.

AlphaGenome Atlas is a 1PB dataset containing every single possible nucleotide variant alongside an AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score. This score helps researchers instantly understand the potential impact of any given variation.

AlphaGenome Atlas is available to researchers around the world, with coding and non-coding variations available.

snippet.title: The city that sank into the sea in 2 minutes — Port Royal 1692 🌍
snippet.description:
Port Royal 1692 liquefaction earthquake sunken city Jamaica Pompeii Caribbean
On June 7th 1692 a magnitude 7.5-8.0 earthquake struck Port Royal Jamaica. Soil liquefaction caused entire city blocks to sink underwater while still standing. In 2 minutes two thirds of the city were submerged. 5,000 total deaths. On the floor of Kingston Bay the 17th century city still exists — streets, buildings, everyday objects, clocks stopped at the exact time of the earthquake. The Pompeii of the Caribbean.
Does the history or the archaeology fascinate you more?
